title: Power and Progress
subtitle: Our Thousand-Year Struggle over Technology and Prosperity
pitch: Two economists, later Nobel laureates, show that new technology only helps most people when power is shared, and argue AI is heading the wrong way.

chapters.g: A thousand years of history show that technology often enriched a small elite while others gained little.
The common belief that gains from technology always trickle down to workers, and when it fails.
Periods like the post war decades, when unions, democracy and policy spread the gains.
Technology helps workers when it creates new tasks for them, not only when it replaces them.
Much AI replaces workers without big productivity gains, and boosts surveillance.
Policies to steer AI towards helping workers: tax reform, worker voice, breaking up big tech and more.

ideas: Technology's benefits depend on who holds power.
Trickle down from productivity is not guaranteed.
Machine usefulness, not machine intelligence, should be the goal.
AI's direction can and should be steered.

args.a: AI is mostly being used to automate and surveil, not to help workers.
args.c: Others point to AI tools that raise the skills and output of less experienced workers.
Critics doubt governments can pick the right direction for innovation.

questions: Who has gained most from the technology in your life?
What would worker friendly AI look like in your job?
Should AI development be steered by policy?

quiz.q: What do the authors say decides who benefits from technology?

o: Automation that replaces workers with only small productivity gains

quiz.q: What prize did both authors later win?
